description: A fleet-scoped Jamf Pro API client secret arrives in Parameter 6, and the bearer token goes on curl's command line. Tests Credential severity, the Platform + Deployment origin, and the distinct-issue test for two exposures with different fixes.

findings.rationale: Q1, Credential severity: 'Jamf parameter $4-$11, while a policy populates it' with fleet-wide write scope (the README's API role has Update Computers and the policy is scoped to All Computers) gives High, Origin Platform + Deployment. The code accepts the secret only through Parameter 6, so the populated-parameter rating is the headline (Credential severity, second bullet). Adjustments never apply to credential rows.

The bearer token is passed with --oauth2-bearer on curl's command line, so every local user can read it in ps while curl runs (SKILL.md Step 4, Secrets: Authorization headers on the command line). Q4: matches the High example 'curl -u admin:pass visible in ps' (same sink, same gain: a credential with Update Computers scope). Origin Code. It is a separate issue from the Parameter 6 exposure: no single edit closes both (distinct-issue test 5).

rationale: Two High findings give 100 - 40 = 60, inside the High range (25-69). The client secret itself goes to curl on stdin through the printf builtin, so it is not on any command line; a finding that says it is would be a false positive.
